map_note.t: Arizona has nine U.S. House districts, drawn by the voter-created Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission (two Democrats, two Republicans, an independent chair). Its post-2020 map, first used in 2022, is unchanged for 2026. Axios (Aug 2025) reported that the commission cannot redraw mid-decade without a court order, that no challenge was pending, and that the divided Legislature/governor could not put a new map in place for 2026. No 2026 Senate race. Governor and lieutenant governor run as a joint ticket for the first time under Proposition 131 (2022), and the new lieutenant governor office takes effect in January 2027. The partisan primary was July 21, 2026, and the official statewide canvass was Aug 6, 2026. All 15 county post-primary hand counts were within the acceptable margin. No automatic recount was reported for any governor or U.S. House primary, and no source checked mentions one. In the No Labels governor primary, Lytle conceded on July 22 after trailing Hourihan by about 1,200 votes. Early ballots mailed Oct 7. The general is Nov 3, with the statewide canvass Nov 23.

AZ-GOV.note: First Arizona governor's race with joint tickets: Proposition 131 (2022) created a lieutenant governor, and each nominee had to name a running mate. Andy Biggs won the July 21 Republican primary with about 73% over fellow Rep. David Schweikert. Teri Ann Hourihan beat chair-backed Hugh Lytle for the No Labels nomination. The Arizona Green Party opposes its own nominee, Risa Lombardo, as a 'sham' candidate. The party's Aug 31 request to remove her was refused: the Secretary of State said removal needs a court order or her withdrawal. Two Republican write-ins (Gertritrude Gonzalez, Alice Novoa) are not on the printed ballot.

research_notes: FINAL BALLOT SOURCE: the Secretary of State's general-election candidate listing (apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/Election/69), its write-in/withdrawn list (azsos.gov/media/718) and the Aug 6 statewide canvass PDF were identified on azsos.gov, but the fetch tool refused them on provenance grounds, and curl is blocked by the egress proxy. The ballot is therefore verified from two independent secondary listings that agree name for name: The Green Papers (accessed Oct 8) and FOX 10 Phoenix's general-election guide (updated Oct 6, 2026), cross-checked with Wikipedia for primary results.

LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR: the task brief said Arizona has no lieutenant governor. That is no longer true for this election. Proposition 131 (2022) created the office, and 2026 is the first election in which governor candidates run with a running mate (AZ Family Aug 11, 2026; Wikipedia; Ballotpedia). Running mates are therefore recorded: Hobbs–John Giles, Biggs–Sine Kerr, Lombardo–Lisa Castillo (from The Green Papers and FOX 10 only), Hourihan–Angela Harrolle Mohan.

GREEN PARTY DISPUTE: the Arizona Green Party calls governor nominee Risa Lombardo and secretary-of-state nominee Duwayne Collier 'sham' candidates. The Arizona Mirror (via KJZZ, Jul 30) documented Republican ties and a shared Nevada vendor. On Aug 31 the party asked the Secretary of State to replace them with write-ins Carlos Melendez and Jon Ralston, and the office said it cannot remove nominees without a court order or withdrawal. As of the Oct 6 FOX 10 report, Lombardo remains the ballot's Green nominee. Whether Clean Elections' review of qualifying contributions leads to any disqualification is unresolved, so a human should check status before publication. The party also lists CD3 nominee David Redkey as 'actively opposed.'

NO LABELS LABEL: the party's attempt to rename itself 'Arizona Independent Party' (approved by the Secretary of State effective Dec 1, 2025) was ruled invalid (Mar 25, 2026), and an appeal is pending after the midterms. Hourihan and Aversa are listed as No Labels. Tisha Benoit (CD4) filed under 'Arizona Independent Party,' and FOX 10 shows no party label for her, so her printed label needs a check against a sample ballot. All three are coded 'I' per the module convention.

CD1 DISCREPANCY: Wikipedia lists Christopher Ajluni (No Labels) among CD1 general-election candidates, with no primary result. Neither The Green Papers nor FOX 10 (Oct 6) lists him, so he is excluded. Needs an official-list check.

CD3 DISCREPANCY: Wikipedia shows write-in Nicholas Glenn winning the Republican primary with 437 votes. Neither The Green Papers nor FOX 10 lists him for November; they list Jacob Parkman as a Republican write-in. Glenn may not have met the write-in nomination threshold, but this was not confirmed, so he is excluded.
Gary Swing (CD6) and David Redkey (CD3) won Green nominations as primary write-ins (29 and 5 votes). Both appear as Green ballot nominees in The Green Papers and FOX 10.

David Redkey: the arrest and charges (threatening or intimidating; computer tampering) come from AZ Family (Sep 21) and FOX 10. Charges only, with no plea or conviction reported, and the arrest documents were sought sealed. Ballot status after the arrest is not separately confirmed; FOX 10 (Oct 6) still lists him.

Mark Lamb: Wikipedia reports sexual-misconduct and abuse-of-power accusations, which he denies, and a Pinal County Attorney's review that found no evidence of criminal conduct. This rests on one secondary source and was left out of his oneliner pending a second independent source.

Ratings: Cook was read directly (House Sep 25, 2026; governor Oct 1, 2026). The Inside Elections and Sabato ratings are from Wikipedia and mostly dated mid-2025, so they are likely stale for competitive seats (AZ-01, AZ-06, governor). The forecasters' own pages could not be fetched. 270toWin's Oct 2 consensus and Ballotpedia's summaries are added for context.

Campaign sites and FEC ids come from The Green Papers; neither the sites nor the FEC pages were opened in this pass. Goodwin (CD2) and Benoit (CD4) have no listed FEC id. Swing (CD6) has two candidate ids listed and is left null.

Running-mate deadline: the Arizona Capitol Times said the Secretary of State set a Friday deadline (Aug 7) to name running mates. The Arizona Mirror (Jul 31) said Hobbs had until Sept 4. Not reconciled.
Photos not researched in this pass; photo fields are blank, not guessed.

Write-ins (not on the printed ballot, so not in candidates): Governor — Gertritrude Gonzalez (R), Alice Novoa (R); CD1 — Dev Gupta (I), Gage Dylan Thunder; CD3 — Jacob Parkman (R); CD4 — Steven Sanders (No Labels); CD6 — Michael Dorland (I); CD9 — G. Seville Hatch (I), William Perry (I). Sources: The Green Papers and FOX 10.
